instructions: Fill a large pot with water, add the salt and bring it to a boil over high heat.
Cut the crusts off 3 slices of bread. Tear the soft inside into pea-size crumbs with your fingers. That should be about 1 1/2 cups.

Heat 3 tbsp of the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the crumbs and stir all the time for 4 to 5 minutes, until they're golden and crisp. Transfer them to a bowl and wipe out the skillet.
Add the spaghetti to the boiling water. Cook for 10 minutes, or as the box says, until it's tender with a little bite.
Meanwhile, chop the 4 anchovy fillets and mince the garlic. Chop 1/4 cup of the parsley.
Heat the remaining 2 tbsp olive oil in the skillet over medium-low heat. Add the anchovies and stir for 2 minutes, until they melt into the oil.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, until it smells sweet. Don't let it brown. Browned garlic turns bitter.
Scoop out 1 cup of the pasta water, then drain the spaghetti.
Add the spaghetti to the skillet with 1/2 cup of the pasta water. Toss over medium-low heat for 1 minute, until the oil and water cling to the pasta. Add more pasta water if it looks dry.
Take the skillet off the heat. Stir in half of the crumbs and the chopped parsley.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with the rest of the crumbs sprinkled over the top and the red pepper flakes at the table.
method_notes: The lead (The Pasta Project, 5 stars from 46 ratings) melts anchovy and garlic in olive oil, tosses it with the pasta and a little cooking water, and finishes with crumbs fried until crisp. Taste of the Place agrees on the method but adds lemon zest and a lot of parsley. This version keeps the lead's amounts, uses the soft inside of the bread as both sources say, and puts the red pepper flakes on the table. Choose a bread without milk in it to keep this dairy-free.
